About IAWH Health

We exist because the healthcare system was not built with every woman in mind. We are building the organization that should have existed all along.

Who We Are

Advancing women's health. One woman at a time.

The Institute for the Advancement of Women's Health (IAWH) is a Virginia-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization. We were founded on a conviction that women deserve healthcare systems, information, and community that see them as whole people, not just collections of reproductive organs or chronic conditions.

Our mission is to broaden the understanding of women's health beyond reproductive and sexual health, raising awareness and increasing knowledge about a woman as a whole person, considering her sociology and the many social determinants that shape her health and well-being.

We connect rural, urban, suburban, and multicultural women of all ages with evidence-based information to support informed healthcare decision-making. We conduct and apply community-based public health research that leads to women becoming more knowledgeable and better-informed participants in their own care.

Our Approach

Evidence. Community. Equity.

Everything IAWH builds is grounded in three principles that shape how we work, what we publish, and who we serve.

01

Evidence First

Every program IAWH delivers and every article the journal publishes is grounded in verifiable evidence. We do not promote wellness trends or unproven interventions. We take the research seriously, translate it into plain language, and stand behind what we publish.

02

Community Centered

IAWH listens before it builds. Our programs are developed with community input, tested in community settings, and designed to meet women where they are, not where a healthcare system assumes them to be. The women we serve are partners, not patients.

03

Equity Driven

Health disparities are not random. They are the predictable result of systems that were designed without certain communities in mind. IAWH names that clearly and builds programs that address it directly, with particular attention to the health needs of Black women and women in underserved communities.

Leadership

The people behind the work.

Cheryl J. Thompson, MSPH

Co-Founder and Executive Director

Cheryl J. Thompson is a public health practitioner, health equity advocate, and the Co-Founder and Executive Director of IAWH Health. She holds a Master of Science in Public Health and brings deep expertise in chronic disease management, women's health, and the intersection of social determinants with health outcomes.

Cheryl co-founded IAWH Health with Janine Payne, MPH, on the conviction that community-based public health research and plain-language health journalism could shift the relationship between women and their own healthcare. Under her leadership, IAWH has developed HeartStrong℠ Community, launched a monthly health journal now reaching nearly 600 subscribers, and cultivated partnerships with leading academic and healthcare institutions across the country.

The organization has mentored nine American University Public Health Scholars through IAWH's long-standing field placement partnership, guiding students through real-world research, health communications, and program development that goes well beyond the classroom.
